subject: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (post-demo)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodai.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (post-demo)

Hi Sana / Marcus 1

Great to meet you both on the demo today. Quick recap and next steps on the items you asked about during the call (PII handling, retention, logging, and third-party subprocessors):

1) Subprocessors: I've attached our current third-party/subprocessor list (redwood_subprocessors_list_2027-05.pdf). This includes telemetry vendors, cloud infra providers, and marketplace integrations. We update this quarterly; let me know if you need an alternate format.

2) Data residency: Hosted (Redwood API) currently offers region controls for data in US and EU regions. For enterprise/private deployments we can accommodate on-prem / customer VPC where data does not leave your environment.

3) PII & retention: Default retention for logs/telemetry is 30 days for hosted tenants; configurable for Dedicated/Private. We can redact prompts at ingestion and support customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM) for Private deployments.

4) Logging & access controls: We provide token-level access logs in the Console, role-based access controls, and audit exports. See attached SOC2 report for controls.

Next steps I propose:
- Share the attached subprocessors list & SOC2 PDF (attached).
- Loop in our security lead Neha for any technical follow-up (cc'd here).
- If this looks good, propose a short procurement/terms call to walk contract redlines next week.

Do these next steps work or do you want more detail on any specific vendor/sharing flow?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: [redwood_subprocessors_list_2027-05.pdf, SOC2_type2_report_2027.pdf]

From: Sana Patel <sana@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (post-demo)

Thanks Marissa 1

Helpful recap. A couple of clarifying questions before we loop legal/procurement: 

- Can you confirm which telemetry vendors collect aggregated usage metrics vs any that receive request-level content? We need assurance that no PHI or identifiable PII will be sent to third parties.

- For cloud providers: would our production data ever be stored in a different country for routing/failover reasons? We need a clear policy for data residency for HIPAA scope.

- On retention: is the 30-day default applied to both prompt inputs and model-generated outputs/logs? We may require a 7-day retention for a pilot scope.

If you can send those specifics and the SOC2, we'll prep a short internal summary for legal. Also include any DocuSign/contract links if you're planning to provide initial terms.

Best,
Sana
Senior Product Manager, Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodai.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@acmehealth.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (post-demo)

Hi Sana 1

Thanks for the great questions. Looping Neha (Security) and David (SE) to provide authoritative answers. Quick summary answers while they chime in: 

- Telemetry vendors: Most of our telemetry is aggregated (metrics, performance). We have a small set of vendors that process request-level traces for debugging (e.g., error traces), but we do not send request payloads to telemetry vendors by default. See attached redwood_datasharing_telemetry_matrix.xlsx which marks vendors and the type of data shared. If you need no request-level exports, we can disable those integrations for your tenant.

- Cloud providers/data residency: For Redwood hosted API, persistent storage of data for current customers in the US is in US regions only (we use AWS us-west-2 / us-east-1). Disaster recovery replicas are also within the same region family unless specified otherwise in an enterprise contract. For EU customers we use EU-only regions. For any cross-region failover we surface options in the contract. For HIPAA scopes we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments.

- Retention: The 30-day default applies to logs and request/response traces retained for debugging. Prompt inputs and generated outputs are retained per tenant config; for hosted customers we can set a 7-day retention for the pilot if that's required. For Private/Dedicated, retention is customer-configurable.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessors_list_2027-05.pdf, SOC2_type2_report_2027.pdf, redwood_datasharing_telemetry_matrix.xlsx

Neha / David: can you confirm the telemetry vendor list and add any notes re: PHI/PII redaction options and whether any of our marketplace partners receive request-level content?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: [redwood_subprocessors_list_2027-05.pdf, SOC2_type2_report_2027.pdf, redwood_datasharing_telemetry_matrix.xlsx]

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodai.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@acmehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodai.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: data handling & subprocessors (post-demo)

Hi Sana 1

Quick security confirmation from my side: 

- PHI/PII: We support prompt redaction and tokenization at ingestion. For hosted customers, we offer an option to drop PII at the edge before it's sent to our runtime, and we can also enable additional scrubbing pipelines. For customers requiring HIPAA-level controls we recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-controlled KMS.

- Telemetry vendors: The attached matrix denotes which telemetry providers receive aggregated metrics vs request-level error traces. No vendor receives full request payloads by default. If Acme wants zero request-level exports, we will disable error-trace forwarding and provide in-house debugging options.

- Marketplace partners: Marketplace connectors (e.g., analytics plugins) are listed in the subprocessors PDF; none of our default marketplace partners ingest request payloads unless explicitly configured by the customer.

- Next steps: If the above meets your requirements, we can: (1) provide a short exception/controls statement for your legal team, (2) prepare a procurement packet and a DocuSign link with starter terms, and (3) schedule a 30-min call with David to go through integration controls.

Let me know which of those you want to prioritize.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security Lead | Redwood Inference
attachments: [redwood_datasharing_telemetry_matrix.xlsx]
